page: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a single dedicated physical core and vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. However, due to its single-vCPU configuration, multi-core and parallel processing benchmarks like multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core score rank in the lower percentiles. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is average, while read-only memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is relatively poor. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, whereas database operations and static web serving throughput are on the lower end.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7a.medium offers a low-entry point to the memory-optimized AMD EPYC Gen7 family, delivering dedicated CPU resources and DDR5 memory without the overhead of larger multi-core instances. This makes it suitable for lightweight, memory-sensitive workloads that do not require high parallel processing power, such as small-scale caching, single-threaded data processing, basic database operations, or lightweight text processing tasks.
